claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure comprising a continuous fcc matrix and dispersed C14 Laves precipitates.
The intrinsic orbital moment of the fcc phase remains limited.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys have coercivity capped at approximately 100 Oe because of insufficient orbital moments.
Strong antiferromagnetic exchange coupling occurs between Fe/Co moments in the fcc matrix and a Ti-rich sublattice in the C14 phase.
Antiferromagnetic interfacial coupling aligns fcc-phase moments antiparallel to moments associated with the Ti sublattice.
The fcc/C14 coupling creates an interfacial magnetic dead layer.
Interfacial moment compensation lowers the saturation magnetization of the fcc grains.
The C14 phase has strong magnetic anisotropy.
Local anisotropy and strain fields at fcc/C14 interfaces create deep energy barriers for domain-wall motion.
The fcc/C14 interfaces act as effective domain-wall pinning sites.
The proposed interfacial mechanisms increase coercivity despite the limited intrinsic orbital moment of the fcc phase.
The dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy exhibits approximately 667 Oe coercivity at 400 K.
At 400 K, the dual-phase alloy has lower saturation magnetization than a corresponding pure fcc alloy because of interfacial compensation.
A C14-dominant FeCoNiTi alloy will show a distinct magnetic transition near either 168 K or 214 K.
A C14-dominant alloy will show negligible coercivity enhancement relative to the dual-phase alloy.
The proposed coupling mechanism requires a coherent or semi-coherent fcc/C14 interface and may fail at fully incoherent or amorphous boundaries.
The coercivity enhancement may diminish above the Curie temperature of the C14 phase.
Changing C14 volume fraction and annealing history can vary the fcc/C14 interfacial area while retaining the relevant phases.
Spin-polarized DFT on a coherent fcc(111)/C14(0001) interface can test the sign and magnitude of interfacial exchange and the fcc-side spin density of states at the Fermi level.
Comparing single-phase fcc, dual-phase, and C14-dominant samples can isolate whether magnetic transitions and coercivity arise from the individual phases or their interfaces.
